title: Build a Headless Site: Content in Orchard Core, Front End Anywhere | Orchard Core
description:
A site can keep its content in Orchard Core and leave the pages to another application: a web app, a static site or a mobile app. That front end needs an API to read the content, permission to call it, and a way for the browser to accept the answer.

This video builds that on a Blog site. It enables GraphQL, explores the API in GraphiQL, shows how a saved query becomes a GraphQL field, grants the Anonymous role the permissions to run it, and adds a CORS policy so a page on its own address can read the posts.

In this video:
• How a headless site works
• Enable the GraphQL and CORS Configuration features
• Explore the API in GraphiQL
• How a saved query becomes a GraphQL field
• Grant the Anonymous role the permissions to call it
• Call the endpoint from a page on its own address
• Add a CORS policy so the browser accepts the answer
• Recipes, limits and sign-in for a production site
